rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Falsehood against God includes fabricated prophethood like Musaylima and al-Aswad al-Ansi, inventing religion and rulings like Amr b. Luhay, or any unworthy attribution to God.
rows.anchor: Müseylimetü’l-kezzâb ve Esved-i Ansî gibi “Allah beni peygamber gönderdi” diye yalandan nübüvvet iddia etmeye

words: أُوحِىَ إِلَىَّ وَلَمْ يُوحَ إِلَيْهِ شَىْءٌۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause may mean claiming revelation when none came, or claiming it for oneself while denying revelation to the Prophet, thus combining the two great kinds of lie.
rows.anchor: Yalanın iki büyük nev‘ini cem‘etmiş, yoğa var, vara yok diye muzâ‘af bir kizb-i azîm söylemiş demek olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Taifian Nadr b. Harith and associates claimed they could match the Qur’an, citing 8:31 and reciting a ridiculous parody about sowing, baking, cooking, and eating.
rows.anchor: Allah’a rekabet, Kur’ân’ı tanzir, peygambere mu‘âraza edeceği zu‘munda bulunmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited incidents occasioned this verse; since some occurred in Mecca and others in Medina, it is reported as Medinan while also pointing to Meccan events.
rows.anchor: bu âyetin de Mekke hâdisâtına dahi işaret ederek Medine’de nâzil olduğu mervîdir

words: وَلَوْ تَرَىٰٓ إِذِ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ فِى غَمَرَٰتِ ٱلْمَوْتِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scene shows these wrongdoers plunged into death’s agonies as angels reach toward them and order them to bring out their souls or save themselves, before a humiliating punishment.
rows.anchor: melekler ellerini uzatarak {أَخْرِجُوٓا۟ أَنفُسَكُمُ} haydi bakalım canlarınızı çıkarın yahud kendinizi kurtarın

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their arrogance toward God’s signs means they could not stomach belief in them and avoided believing and reflecting on them.
rows.anchor: kibrinize yediremiyor, onlara imandan, teemmülden kaçınıyordunuz

words: جِئْتُمُونَا فُرَٰدَىٰ كَمَا خَلَقْنَٰكُمْ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At resurrection each person comes alone, just as created the first time, having left behind all the possessions God had granted.
rows.anchor: bugün bize ilk defa sizi halk ettiğimiz gibi teker teker, yalnız başınıza geldiniz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The supposed intercessors are absent; people had imagined them partners in their existence, holding a share in lordship and interceding for them with God.
rows.anchor: Mevcûdiyetiniz üzerinde bunların rubûbiyet hissesine mâlik birtakım şürekâ olduklarını ve Allah’a karşı size şefaat edeceklerini zannediyordunuz

rows.speaker: نافع، حفص، كسائي، أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Readers other than Nafi, Hafs, Kisai, and Abu Ja‘far read baynakum with the nūn raised; the author renders this as the permanent severing of all ties between them.
rows.anchor: Nâfi‘, Hafs, Kisâî, Ebû Cafer’den mâ‘adâsında nûn’un ref‘iyle بَيْنَكُمْ okunduğuna göre

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address declares that the bonds between them have been severed forever and their former imagined supports have vanished.
rows.anchor: artık aranız ebediyyen açıldı, bütün râbıtalar kesildi, târumâr oldu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imagined partners and intercessors prove to be delusions that have disappeared from them.
rows.anchor: zu‘m etmiş olduğunuz o hayaller, o kuruntular sizden gayb oldu gitti

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People should picture this reckoning and avoid injustice and failure to recognize God’s due.
rows.anchor: Bunları göz önüne getirmeli de Allah’a karşı haksızlıkta, takdirsizlikte bulunmamalıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam and Eve may eat where they wish, but their permission is bounded; the forbidden tree marks a limit rather than granting unlimited freedom or ownership.
rows.anchor: bu salâhiyet ve me’zûniyet her kayıttan âzâde gayr-i mahdûd bir hürriyet ve temlik olmayıp

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A tree marks a spatial boundary and eating its fruit a limit on action; although within paradise, its vicinity became a testing ground for Adam and Eve.
rows.anchor: Haddinizi tecavüz ve kendinize yazık etmiş bulunursunuz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam remained subject to obligation even in paradise; transgressing the limits and rights God set makes anyone unjust to himself.
rows.anchor: Âdem’in cennette bile mebde’-i mükellefiyetten âzâde olmadığını

words: لِيُبْدِىَ لَهُمَا مَا وُۥرِىَ عَنْهُمَا مِن سَوْءَٰتِهِمَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Until then Adam and Eve neither saw nor knew the shameful parts of themselves or each other; God had initially concealed them.
rows.anchor: Âdem ve Havvâ bu lahzaya kadar hilkatlerinde kendilerini utandıracak ve tiksindirecek çirkin pis şeylere mahall-i sudûr ve zuhûr olacak kötü yerlerini ne kendilerinden ne de birbirlerinden görmüyorlar ve hatta bilmiyorlardı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report says a light kept their private parts hidden from their sight.
rows.anchor: Bir rivayete göre bir nûr ile nazarlarından mestur idi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report says their shame was concealed by a covering like a fingernail.
rows.anchor: diğer bir rivayette de tırnak kabîlinden bir örtü ile mestur idi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person cannot fully know even the parts already within his own body; human nature can develop toward good or evil according to obedience to the limits God sets after creation.
rows.anchor: hilkatinin bütün kuvveleri şöyle dursun, bilfiil muhtevî olduğu eczâsına bile tamamen vâkıf olamaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though created in the best form, humans can disobey once will appears and fall to the lowest state; religion and divine command protect them, while Satan seeks that fall by exposing their shame.
rows.anchor: din ve emr-i ilâhî insanlığı bu sukūttan muhafazaya müteveccih olduğu gibi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waswasa originally means a faint rustling, hissing, or whispering sound; repeated hidden inward speech, and inducing such speech in someone, are also called waswasa.
rows.anchor: “Vesvese” asl-ı lügatta hışırtı, fışırtı, fısıltı gibi savt-ı hafî demektir

words: أَن تَكُونَا مَلَكَيْنِ أَوْ تَكُونَا مِنَ ٱلْخَٰلِدِينَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan tempted them with becoming angels free from eating and drinking or becoming immortal, stirring envy of angels and desire for eternal life through a material cause.
rows.anchor: bundan yerseniz ya yemek içmek ihtiyacından melekler gibi müstağnî olursunuz, yahut ölüm yüzü görmez, müebbed kalırsınız

rows.speaker: أعاظم المفسرين
rows.claim: A popular story says Satan entered paradise by means of a snake, but eminent exegetes considered this explanation weak and offered three alternatives.
rows.anchor: hayye vâsıtasıyla girdi diye bir kıssa nakli şöhret bulmuş ise de bunu e‘âzım-ı müfessirîn rekîk addetmişler

rows.speaker: حسن البصري
rows.claim: Hasan al-Basri says God gave Satan power to convey whispers from earth to heaven or paradise; the author suggests snake may figuratively mean a venomous life force in humans.
rows.anchor: Hasan-ı Basrî Hazretleri demiştir ki Allah teâlâ’nın vermiş olduğu bir kuvvet ile yerden semâya veya cennete vesvese îsâl edebilmiştir

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم الأصفهاني
rows.claim: Abu Muslim al-Isfahani holds that this was an earthly garden where Adam and Iblis were both present; the author says this plainly does not answer how Satan whispered.
rows.anchor: Ebû Müslim İsfahânî bu cennetin Arz cennetlerinden biri olduğuna kāil olduğu için “Âdem ve İblis ikisi de cennette idi” demiş, lâkin bunun suâle muntabık olmadığı zâhirdir

rows.speaker: بirtakım müفسرين
rows.claim: Other exegetes say Adam and Eve sometimes came near paradise’s gate, while Satan watched and approached from outside to whisper to them.
rows.anchor: Diğer birtakım müfessirîn de demişlerdir ki Âdem ve Havvâ bazen cennetin kapısına yakın gelirler, İblis de hâriçten gözetir yaklaşırdı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verses indicate that Satan’s expulsion did not remove his ability to whisper from the four directions.
rows.anchor: İblis’in tard ve ihrâcı cihât-ı erba‘adan ilkā-i vesvese imkânını selbeder bir surette olmadığı anlaşılıyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan swore that he was their sincere adviser, deceiving them into descending from purity to eating the tree; they thought no one would swear falsely by God.
rows.anchor: Âdem ve Havvâ hiçbir kimse yalan yere Allah’a yemin etmez sandılar, aldandılar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As soon as they tasted the tree, the shameful parts hidden from them became visible; the ill consequence of disobedience appeared, and they began covering themselves from shame with paradise leaves.
rows.anchor: Masiyetin şeâmeti yüz gösterdi, mestur ve mahfî olan avret mahalleri açılıverdi, bunun üzerine hayâlarından

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is reported that the leaves they used to cover themselves were fig leaves.
rows.anchor: Denilmiş ki bu yaprak incir yaprağı idi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s rebuke has two parts: they disobeyed the prohibition and were taken in by the warning about their enemy.
rows.anchor: evvelkisi nehye muhalefetlerinden dolayı, ikincisi de düşman sözüne aldanmalarından dolayı itâb ve tevbihtir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although this warning is not stated explicitly earlier in al-A‘raf, the question here implies it had been given, and Ta-Ha 20:117 states it explicitly.
rows.anchor: bu sûrede sarâhaten sebk etmemiş ise de

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Libas is clothing that covers shameful parts; rish means adornment, finery, or wealth and prosperity.
rows.anchor: muhakkak ki Biz üzerinize fena yerlerinizi örter; setr-i avret eder bir libas

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created and bestowed means of clothing and adornment from earthly, heavenly, inward, outward, individual, social, natural, and crafted sources.
rows.anchor: Arzî, semâvî, enfüsî, âfâkî, ferdî, ictimâ‘î, tabîî, sun‘î esbâbını halk u ihsan eyledik

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Like Adam and Eve, each child is protected and covered in the womb, born naked, then enabled to cover, protect, and adorn the body with poorer or richer clothing.
rows.anchor: rahm-i mâderde “meşîme” içinde mahfuz ve mestur olarak merzuk olup dururken çırçıplak yeryüzüne indiler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The garment of taqwa is God-consciousness, shame, and reverent awe; by God’s permission it protects against moral and physical shame, harm, and ruin.
rows.anchor: hiss-i hayâ ve haşyetullah ile giyilen ve biiznillah maddî mânevî ayıptan, fenalıktan, zarar ve mehlekeden vikāye edecek olan korunmak elbisesi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The taqwa garment is absolute good and pure benefit; it is the true purpose and benefit of clothing.
rows.anchor: hayr-ı mutlaktır, nef‘-i mahzdır. Elbise nimetinden tena‘‘um ve istifade asıl bununladır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pious cover their shame even if naked, as Adam and Eve covered themselves with leaves, while the wicked remain exposed in shame however well dressed.
rows.anchor: Âdem ve Havvâ’nın yapraklarla tesettür ettikleri gibi ayıp ve avretlerini setr ü muhafaza ederler. Fakat hiss-i takvâsı olmayan fâcirler ne kadar giyinseler yine kıçları açılmaktan kurtulamazlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Clothing should cover nakedness, protect from heat, cold, harmful things, disease, and enemies, and adorn modestly without provoking lust or disgust.
rows.anchor: elbise nimetinin ayıp ve avreti setr

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People who wear finery from lust, pride, and vanity may expose their worst parts and incur unexpected harm; outward finery is a divine blessing but often becomes vanity’s commodity.
rows.anchor: rîş, libas, fahr u ihtişam dahi haddizâtında bir ni‘met-i ilâhiye olmakla beraber birçoklarının gözlerini kamaştıran câzibe-i zâhiriyesine rağmen hayr ve nef‘-i mahz değil, bir metâ‘-ı gurûrdur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Clothing is one of God’s signs, evidence of His kindness and mercy; people should reflect on its wisdom, remember His blessings, and take heed by avoiding indecencies.
rows.anchor: Me’muldür ki bunu tezekkür ederler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse warns Adam’s descendants not to be seduced and expelled as their parents were; Satan and his clan see people from where people cannot see them, and are patrons of unbelievers.
rows.anchor: Babanızla ananızı çirkin yerlerini kendilerine göstermek için Şeytan cennetten çıkardığı gibi sakının sizi de belâya uğratmasın

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People excuse indecency by citing their ancestors and falsely attributing it to God, but God does not command indecency and they must not attribute what they do not know to Him.
rows.anchor: “atalarımızı böyle bulduk ve bize bunu Allah emretti” derler. “Allah” de, “edepsizliği emretmez, bilmediğiniz şeyleri Allah’ın üzerine mi atıyorsunuz?”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God commands justice, worship with faces rightly oriented at every mosque and sincere religion devoted to Him, and promises that people will return as He first created them.
rows.anchor: Rabbim adl ü insâfı emretti. Hem her mescidde yüzlerinizi doğru tutun ve O’na, dini mahza O’nun için hâlis kılarak ibadet edin. Sizi ibtidâ O yarattığı gibi yine O’na döneceksiniz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God guided some and made error due for others because they adopted satans as patrons instead of God while imagining themselves guided.
rows.anchor: Bir kısmına hidâyet buyurdu, bir kısmına da dalâlet hak oldu. Çünkü bunlar Allah’ı bırakıp şeytanları evliyâ ittihaz ettiler, bir de kendilerini hidâyette zannederler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says non-Ḥums Bedouins performed naked tawaf, refusing clothes worn in disobedience; men usually went by day and women at night, sometimes by day with almost no covering, reciting a woman’s poem; the verses were revealed for this practice.
rows.anchor: yani bedevîler Beyt-i Şerîf’i üryan oldukları hâlde tavaf ederler
